stem.text: Let R be the region that lies inside the polar curve \( r = 7 - 4 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} \) and outside the circle \( r = \frac{15}{2} \). The curves intersect at \( \theta = 3.267 \) and \( \theta = 6.158 \), correct to three decimal places. Using a calculator, find the area of R. Show the setup for the calculation, and give the value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The stated intersection angles are \( 3.267 \) and \( 6.158 \), and between them the limacon is outside the circle, so it is the outer curve.

The area is one half the integral of the difference of the squares of the radii: \( A = \frac{1}{2}\int_{3.267}^{6.158} \left(\left(7 - 4 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}\right)^2 - \frac{225}{4}\right)\,d\theta \).
A calculator gives \( A \approx 57.637 \), using the unrounded intersection angles.

options.derivation: the integral taken over half the region, from the axis of symmetry to one intersection angle, without doubling
the factor of one half left off the integral of the difference of the squares
the square of the difference of the radii integrated in place of the difference of the squares
